nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $p$ be a prime, and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in $Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.
nodes.title: Eulerian polynomial factorization implies $p$-solvability

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$, every prime $p$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ is a product $PQ$ of integer polynomials where $P$ involves no variable other than $x_p$ and $x_p$ does not occur in $Q$, then $G$ is $p$-solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(b) (Eulerian polynomials and $p$-solvability)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\varphi$ be an Eulerian function of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$. If there are a finite set $S$ of primes and, for each $q \in S$, an integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$, such that the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Solvability from one-variable factorizations of the Eulerian polynomial

nodes.summary: This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every Eulerian function $\varphi$ of $G$, with values in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$: if there are a finite set $S$ of primes and, for each $q \in S$, an integer polynomial $P_q$ involving no variable other than $x_q$, such that the Eulerian polynomial $\varphi(G)$ equals $\prod_{q \in S} P_q$, then $G$ is solvable.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.104(a) (Eulerian polynomials and solvability, G. E. Wall)

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $f$ be the order polynomial. A function $\varphi$ from the subgroups of $G$ to the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$ is an Eulerian function of $G$ if $\sum_{K \le H} \varphi(K) = f(H)$ for every subgroup $H$ of $G$, the sum running over the subgroups $K$ of $H$. The value $\varphi(G)$ is the Eulerian polynomial of $G$.
nodes.title: Eulerian function of a group (G. E. Wall)

nodes.summary: For a natural number $p$, a group $G$ is $p$-solvable if it has a chain of subgroups $1 = N_0 \le N_1 \le \dots \le N_n = G$ in which each $N_i$ is normal in $N_{i+1}$ and each index $[N_{i+1} : N_i]$, taken to be $0$ when it is infinite, is a power $p^k$ with $k \ge 0$ or is coprime to $p$. For finite $G$ and prime $p$ this says that every factor $N_{i+1}/N_i$ is a $p$-group or has order prime to $p$.
nodes.title: $p$-solvable group

nodes.summary: For a subgroup $H$ of a group, the order polynomial of $H$ is $f(H) = \prod_p x_p^{v_p(|H|)}$ in the integer polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[x_0, x_1, \dots]$, where $p$ runs over the primes, $x_p$ is the variable indexed by $p$, and $v_p(|H|)$ is the exponent of $p$ in the order $|H|$ of $H$. If $H$ is infinite, $f(H) = 1$.
nodes.title: Order polynomial of a subgroup
